an3.34:1.1: This short text is surprisingly difficult to interpret exactly, but it helps to think of it as differentiating those deeds that result in rebirth from those that do not.
an3.34:2.1: The text does not use emphatic forms (“any deed”), since some deeds will yield their result in the same life. It is restricted to those deeds that result in rebirth.
an3.34:2.2: The stock phrase on the threefold manifestation of _vipāka_ (see [an6.63:36.2]()) appears superfluous here. Its purpose is normally to establish the places where the results of deeds manifest, yet that is already established in the premise. It seems awkward, if not contradictory, to say there are three places, when the text has already spoken of just one. I suspect it is a later addition to this passage, possibly prompted by taking the passage to be a universal one, which must then account for all possibilities.
an3.34:7.3: I’d prefer to translate as “contentment, love, and understanding”, but the nuances of the following passage call for a more literal rendering.
an3.34:8.1: A deed that is not motivated by greed still results in rebirth, albeit in a happy state. But when greed is done away with by the arahant, it no longer results in rebirth. The point is that, since deeds without greed, hate, and delusion lead to the end of greed, hate, and delusion, there is no need to fear that they will result in kammic consequence.
an3.34:13.5: _Vedaniyaṁ_ here must mean “to be understood” rather than “to be experienced”. The latter would contradict the prose of the Sutta, which specifies rebirth in the next life, as well as the more general understanding of the three possible outcomes of kamma. However, this is not the case, as it applies not to the result—which as it falls under the first noble truth is to be experienced—but to the deed, which falls under the second noble truth, to be given up through understanding.
an3.34:13.6: Here _vatthu_ means the ground or field of kamma that produces future results, as in [sn12.25:14.3]() and [an4.171:5.3](); it is also called the _khetta_ at [an3.76:2.3]().
